findings.text: follow-on: the widened closure_blockers is asserted only for its gate entry and its trailing close op, so two of the three obstacle kinds it lists are asserted nowhere. tests/test_finished_plan_reads_closable.py:132 checks the gate id and :133 its ops, :104 checks the trailing close op, and no assertion and no fixture reaches the section entry with ops [descope] or the followup entry with ops [resolve] that reckon/roadmap.py:860-875 adds. The goal asks for closure_blockers listing every obstacle to close, and a regression that dropped the deferred-section or open-followup entries, or returned the wrong ops for them, leaves all four tests green.

follow-on: the guard at reckon/roadmap.py:833 makes the roadmap's two readers of one question disagree for an empty declaration set, and no comment at the guard says so. plan_executable_remainder documents an empty declaration as a known zero (reckon/_schema.py:805-806: an empty declaration is therefore known zero), and roadmap.implementable_sections documents the absent case as declaring no work rather than unknown (reckon/roadmap.py:106-117), while is_closable reads a present-but-empty mapping as unknown and refuses to call the plan closable. The divergence is load-bearing and disclosed in the landing fragment (metadata_index.readiness_from_state collapses an absent declaration set to an empty mapping, so without the guard every legacy plan would read closable), but a reader of a roadmap row cannot tell the two readers apart, and the comment at the guard states the mechanism of the check rather than why it departs from the owner it calls.

follow-on: the body of commit d8d3b1496303c6e4638d135b9fb36ba462549884 ends with 'The key generator for a closable plan's closure_blockers goes through the same top-level import rather than a literal duplicated here', but nothing in that commit does this: its diff is one hunk at reckon/roadmap.py:818 (the docstring and the not-declarations guard) and one at tests/test_finished_plan_reads_closable.py:58 (the legacy-empty fixture), and the parent commit bee60dba4 already read SECTION_DECLARATION_DEFERRED from the top-level import rather than a literal. A commit body that names a change absent from its own commit misleads the reader who reconstructs the work from git log.

justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/roadmap.py:3321-3325 computes closable from the authored declarations and subtracts it from is_ready and is_blocked as well as from the deferred list, and reckon/roadmap.py:3522 excludes closable slugs from the critical path, so a finished plan leaves ready_now, the blocked set and ready exactly as the goal states.
justifications.reuse: is_closable extends the owner the plan names rather than forking it: the counting is plan_executable_remainder's (reckon/_schema.py:801), and the section predicate under both that owner and roadmap.implementable_sections is is_implementable_section, so no second copy of the predicate is added; the deduction is that the guard at :833 makes is_closable answer an empty mapping differently from roadmap.implementable_sections, giving one module two answers to one question.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --stat 36bbac34495..cfbdda9d lists exactly the five paths the manifest declares and the fence grants, no plan meta line is edited, no figure is written (the done-when names no artifact, so the fragment alone is permitted), and all three commit bodies carry a conventional subject and a body with no plan, sprint or ticket identifier and no attribution trailer.
